name: Leprino Foods Company
old_description: We started in 1950 as a small family-run grocery store in Denver, Colorado. Today, Leprino is proud to be the world’s largest producer of mozzarella cheese and a leading manufacturer of whey protein, lactose, micellar casein and other high-quality dairy ingredients.
about:
Leprino Foods Company began in 1950 as a small family-run grocery store in Denver, Colorado, when Mike Leprino Sr. started making mozzarella cheese by hand in a back room for his family's corner market. The business incorporated as Leprino Cheese Manufacturing Company in the 1960s and adopted the Leprino Foods Company name in the 1970s, remaining family-owned throughout its growth.

Today the company is the world's largest producer of mozzarella cheese and a manufacturer of whey protein, lactose, micellar casein, and other dairy ingredients. Its proprietary processes include the patented "Same Day Dice" method that turns fresh milk into cheese in four hours, and Quality-Locked Cheese that is individually quick-frozen to preserve peak flavor. Operations span manufacturing facilities on three continents, including a 640,000-square-foot plant in Lemoore, California, with over 1,100 employees, and a global headcount exceeding 5,000. Products reach more than 70 countries.

Leprino serves food and nutrition brands worldwide, from major pizza chains and foodservice operators to consumer-packaged-goods manufacturers. A strategic alliance with Dairy Farmers of America secures milk supply, while joint ventures in Europe, Latin America, and Asia Pacific extend its reach. The company also entered the direct-to-consumer market with the Ascent® Protein brand.

The Leprino Difference—rooted in the founder's credo "Leprino Quality is a way of life"—emphasizes quality, service, competitive price, and ethics. The company's stated purpose is to sustainably feed and nourish families globally, guided by a climate-action commitment targeting greenhouse-gas neutrality by 2050.

name: Levine Contract Furniture Group
old_description: Our company was founded by my father, Harvey Levine, in 1973 at a desk in the Pan Am building on 42nd street in New York City. When he opened for business, sales were made in person or on the phone and orders were sent by mail. about:
Levine Contract Furniture Group was founded in 1973 by Harvey Levine at a desk in the Pan Am Building on 42nd Street in New York City. The company began as a one-person operation taking orders by phone and mail. In 1975, John Calvano joined and expanded the sales territory using his personal vehicle. The business remains family-owned and operates from its headquarters in New York City.

The firm acts as a contract furniture dealer and specifier, representing multiple manufacturing partners to furnish corporate, healthcare, education, and retail environments. It maintains an inventory of in-stock products that can ship within 48 hours, ranging from small orders to 50,000-square-foot office installations. The company also provides custom furniture and architectural elements, power and data integration, and privacy pods, managing projects from specification through installation.

Levine serves corporate workplaces, healthcare facilities, educational institutions, and retail spaces. Its portfolio includes open-plan collaboration areas, private offices, conference rooms, huddle rooms, cafés, reception areas, and training rooms. The company emphasizes technology management and durability for educational settings and clinical, public, and professional furnishings for healthcare.

The company differentiates itself through rapid fulfillment of stocked items, a deep understanding of regulated environments such as healthcare, and the ability to deliver bespoke solutions with integrated technology and material selection. Its New York City showroom offers virtual and in-person tours, and the firm provides continuing education units (CEUs) and contract pricing support.

name: Liberate Medical
old_description: VentFree contracts the expiratory muscles during mechanical ventilation to keep them active.
about:
Liberate Medical is based in Crestwood, Kentucky. The company develops and manufactures the VentFree Respiratory Muscle Stimulator, a non-invasive neuromuscular electrical stimulation device designed to contract the abdominal wall muscles in synchrony with exhalation during mechanical ventilation.

The VentFree system uses proprietary stimulation technology that can be initiated from the first day of mechanical ventilation, even while patients are sedated or delirious, without requiring patient cooperation. The device is CE marked for sale throughout the European Economic Area and holds U.S. FDA Emergency Use Authorization to reduce disuse atrophy of the abdominal wall muscles, which may shorten the duration of mechanical ventilation in adult patients, including those with COVID-19.

Liberate Medical serves the critical care and respiratory care markets, targeting hospitals and intensive care units that manage mechanically ventilated patients. Clinical evidence from a pilot randomized controlled trial published in Critical Care (2019) demonstrated that patients receiving VentFree stimulation experienced shorter mechanical ventilation duration and reduced ICU length of stay compared to placebo.

The company positions its technology as a breakthrough approach to preparing patients for weaning from day one of ventilation, aiming to reduce abdominal muscle atrophy—a factor associated with weaning failure and delayed extubation—and potentially lower morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs.

name: Lincoln Electric Products Co.
old_description: We build a full range of highly customizable electrical distribution equipment.
about:
Lincoln Electric Products Co. was founded in 1949 in Union, New Jersey, as a manufacturer of high‑quality electrical distribution equipment serving the tri‑state area. The company remains family‑owned and operated, guided by the core values established by its founder, Irving Leff.

The company produces a full range of highly customizable electrical distribution equipment, including switchboards and integrated electrical systems. All manufacturing takes place in the United States under an ISO 9001:2015‑certified quality management system. The firm emphasizes precision craftsmanship, offering an industry‑two‑year warranty on all equipment, and targets lead times as short as four weeks through experienced project managers and engineers who adapt designs to site‑specific challenges.

Lincoln Electric serves customers across the tri‑state region and beyond, providing tailored electrical solutions for businesses that require reliable power with minimal downtime. Its client base spans industrial, commercial, and institutional sectors, though specific industry verticals are not publicly detailed.

The company differentiates itself through its family‑owned heritage, domestic manufacturing, and a commitment to continuous improvement and on‑time delivery. President Matthew Leff leads a mission focused on collaborative relationships and well‑engineered, high‑quality electrical equipment.

name: Lincoln Industries Manufacturing of WI, LLC
old_description: Lincoln Industries is the largest and most diverse privately-held metal finishing company in North America. We develop technical solutions that move our customers forward by bringing their visions to life.
about:
Lincoln Industries Manufacturing of WI, LLC operates from Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin. The privately held metal finishing company traces its roots back more than seven decades, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed. Ownership remains private, and the company does not name its founders in available materials.

The company specializes in precision electroplating and has been expanding its in-house coating capabilities. Its product portfolio includes a range of truck components such as exhaust systems, bumpers, internal cab parts, grab bars, engine components, emblems, and heat management solutions. In 2025, Lincoln Industries launched Fourth Wall, a new division focused on LED display solutions for sports venues, businesses, and outdoor environments. The company describes itself as the largest and most diverse privately held metal finishing operation in North America, though facility size, headcount, and production volumes are not disclosed.

Lincoln Industries serves customers across agriculture, automotive, appliances, motorsports, powersports, oil and gas, tools, and heavy-duty truck markets. The new Fourth Wall division adds sports entertainment, commercial signage, and outdoor advertising to its industry reach.

The company emphasizes technical solutions that move customers forward, citing its expansion into coating capabilities as a way to deliver enhanced value. Its truck business evolution reflects an ability to embrace complexity and automation, while a stated commitment to wellness and continuous improvement underpins its culture.

name: Lincoln Plastics
old_description: Lincoln Plastics is a Nebraska-based custom extrusion manufacturer.
about:
Lincoln Plastics was founded in 1948 in Lincoln, Nebraska. The company operates as part of the PCE family of companies, alongside its sister division HTI Plastics, which provides injection molding services. No founder names are disclosed.

The company specializes in custom plastic profile extrusion, offering co-extrusion of two materials or colors, flexible and rigid profiles, pipe and tube extrusion, and proprietary Flexiduct cord and cable management systems. Its 25,000-square-foot facility houses in-line quality processes and serves both large and small clients with high production capacity.

Lincoln Plastics serves agricultural irrigation OEMs with components such as drop pipes, hose weights, drive shaft tubes, and PVC U-pipe and U-joint covers. It also supplies office, tradeshow, garage, and home markets with Flexiduct cable management products. Customers are located nationwide and internationally.

The company emphasizes quick order turnaround enabled by its Midwest location, ISO 9001:2015 certification, and a quality management system that includes product-specific quality plans and documented process checks.

name: Little Homestead Furniture
old_description: Solid American Hardwood Furniture, Sofas and Seating since 1987
about: Little Homestead Furniture was founded in 1987 in Rockville, Maryland, by a local architect who opened a showroom dedicated to solid American hardwood furniture. The store carries a range of solid hardwood furniture for every room, including bedroom sets, dining tables, sofas, and home office pieces. Its inventory is sourced from a network of small, family-owned factories in New England—particularly Vermont—as well as manufacturing partners in Pennsylvania, Ohio, Indiana, Texas, North Carolina, and Virginia. A made-to-order program allows customers to modify dimensions, finishes, and features, often at little or no extra cost. Little Homestead primarily serves residential customers in the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area who favor classic, timeless designs such as Shaker, Mission, Arts & Crafts, and contemporary styles. Buyers seek responsibly harvested hardwoods, dovetailed drawers, mortise-and-tenon joinery, and durable environmentally friendly finishes. The founder established the store as an alternative to mass-market furniture that often features distressed or weathered finishes and outsourced production. The emphasis is on well-crafted, real wood furniture made by American wood artisans, offered at reasonable prices with the flexibility of custom modifications.

about:
Loftis Steel & Aluminum, Inc. was founded in 2000 as a family-owned business in Nashville, Tennessee. The company began as a metals distributor and has grown into a regional supplier with a partnership with Tennessee Die Supply, operating from its Nashville facility to serve the Southeast.

The company stocks a diverse inventory of aluminum, steel, and tool steels, and provides in-house processing services including precision laser cutting, waterjet cutting, CAD design and print clean-up, and delivery via its own trucks and shipping partners. Four CAD engineers support customer projects, and the facility emphasizes an employee-centric culture to maintain quality.

Loftis serves a broad range of industries including aerospace, automotive, construction, energy, firearms, government, machine shops, general manufacturing, medical, and oil & gas. Customers range from local machine shops and auto parts manufacturers to government agencies.

name: Logix, LLC
old_description: is to partner with our customers on their electrification journey towards a more sustainable future.
about:
Logix, LLC, founded in 2015 and based in Belfast, Maine, began as SolarLogix, a small family-run solar and heat pump installation company started by Josh and Rachele. The business rebranded to Logix as its service lines expanded to meet growing demand for electrification.

Today the company employs over 35 technicians who install and service heat pumps, solar photovoltaic systems, heat pump water heaters, electric vehicle chargers, battery backup systems, and electrical service upgrades for residential and commercial customers across central and eastern Maine. The firm also provides maintenance, custom quotes, and warranty support.

Logix serves homeowners and businesses seeking to reduce utility costs and carbon emissions through beneficial electrification. The team assists clients with Efficiency Maine rebates, federal tax credits, and USDA REAP grants to offset project costs.

The company states its mission is to partner with customers on their electrification journey toward a more sustainable future, guided by core values of integrity, innovation, resilience, and partnership.

name: Logo Magic
old_description: Logo Magic has been locally owned and operated since 1989 and specializes in custom FR and corporate apparel as well as promotional products to help grow your business. about:
Logo Magic has been locally owned and operated in Dickinson, North Dakota since 1989. The company began as a provider of custom flame‑resistant and corporate apparel, later expanding into promotional products and online store management for businesses, schools, and groups.

The shop runs in‑house screen printing, embroidery, and laser etching equipment to produce decorated apparel such as FR gear, hats, shirts, jackets, and blankets, as well as a wide range of promotional items including bags, drinkware, and office accessories. A graphic design team prepares artwork for each order, and the company also builds and administers temporary e‑commerce storefronts for corporate uniform programs, fundraisers, and team stores. No facility size or headcount figures are published.

Customers range from small businesses and large corporations to schools, clubs, athletic teams, and individuals. The company cites work for corporate uniform programs, fire‑department FR gear, school spirit wear, and personal projects such as family reunion shirts. Vendors supplying blank goods include SanMar, S&S Activewear, Augusta Sportswear, and Richardson Caps.

Logo Magic states its main goal is to deliver a quality product at a competitive price while guiding clients through every step from design to delivery. It emphasizes free custom art services with most apparel orders, quick turnarounds on embroidery and laser‑etched gifts with no minimum quantities, and a hands‑on approach that includes in‑person consultation and doorstep delivery.
